title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulation on Disciplinary Sanctions for Personnel of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions against Court Staff

Fa Fa [2009] No. 61

To all local people's courts at various levels nationwide, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic-level courts, all maritime courts, and all courts at various levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Regulations on Disciplinary Actions against Court Staff are hereby issued for your conscientious implementation. Any issues arising during implementation shall be promptly reported to this Court.

December 31, 2009

Regulations on Disciplinary Actions against Court Staff

Chapter I General Provisions

Section 1 Purpose, Basis, Principles, and Scope of Application

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Public Servants Law of the People's Republic of China and the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of regulating the conduct of court staff, promoting their performance of duties in accordance with the law, and ensuring fair, efficient, and clean administration of justice.

Article 2 Where court staff violate laws, regulations, or the provisions of these Regulations and should bear disciplinary liability, they shall be given disciplinary sanctions in accordance with these Regulations.

Article 3 The conduct of court staff in performing their duties according to law shall be protected by law. No disciplinary sanction shall be imposed except for statutory reasons and through statutory procedures.

Article 4 The following principles shall be adhered to when imposing disciplinary sanctions on court staff:

(1) Seeking truth from facts, objectivity, and fairness;
(2) Equality of all before discipline;
(3) Proportionality of sanctions to the disciplinary violation;
(4) Combining punishment with education.

Article 5 Where court staff commit disciplinary or illegal acts that are suspected of constituting crimes, they shall be referred to the judicial authorities for handling.

Section 2 Types and Application of Disciplinary Sanctions

Article 6 The types of disciplinary sanctions are: warning, demerit, serious demerit, demotion, dismissal from post, and discharge from public employment.

Article 7 The duration of a disciplinary sanction is:

(1) Warning: six months;
(2) Demerit: twelve months;
(3) Serious demerit: eighteen months;
(4) Demotion or dismissal from post: twenty-four months.

Article 8 During the period of a disciplinary sanction, the sanctioned person shall not be promoted in position or rank. In the case of demerit, serious demerit, demotion, or dismissal from post, the sanctioned person shall not be eligible for an increase in pay grade. In the case of dismissal from post, the rank shall be reduced accordingly.

Article 9 For discharge from public employment, from the effective date of the sanction decision, the personnel relationship with the people's court shall be terminated, and the person shall no longer hold any public servant position.

Article 10 Where two or more acts requiring disciplinary sanctions are committed simultaneously, the type of sanction for each act shall be determined separately. If the types of sanctions to be imposed are different, the most severe sanction shall be executed. If several sanctions of the same type below dismissal from post are to be imposed, that sanction shall be executed, and the period of sanction to be served shall be determined between the longest single period and the sum of all periods.

If a new sanction is imposed during the period of another sanction, the total period shall be the sum of the unserved portion of the original period and the new period.

The maximum period of a disciplinary sanction shall not exceed forty-eight months.

Article 11 Where two or more persons jointly commit disciplinary or illegal acts requiring sanctions, each shall be sanctioned according to their respective disciplinary liability.

If the leadership group, relevant organ, or trial organization of a people's court collectively makes a decision to commit or actually commits a disciplinary or illegal act, it shall be handled in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 12 Under any of the following circumstances, a heavier sanction shall be imposed within the range provided in the Specific Provisions of these Regulations:

(1) Playing a principal role in a joint disciplinary or illegal act;
(2) Concealing, forging, or destroying evidence;
(3) Colluding in confessions or preventing others from exposing, reporting, or providing evidence;
(4) Covering up co-offenders;
(5) Other aggravating circumstances provided by laws, regulations, or the Specific Provisions of these Regulations.

Article 13 Under any of the following circumstances, a lighter sanction may be imposed within the range provided in the Specific Provisions of these Regulations:

(1) Voluntarily confessing disciplinary or illegal acts;
(2) Voluntarily taking measures to effectively avoid or recover losses;
(3) Exposing serious disciplinary or illegal acts of others, which are verified as true;
(4) Other mitigating circumstances provided by laws, regulations, or the Specific Provisions of these Regulations.

Article 14 Where a person voluntarily confesses disciplinary or illegal acts and voluntarily takes measures to effectively avoid or recover losses, a sanction one grade lighter than that provided in the Specific Provisions of these Regulations shall be imposed.

Where a warning would otherwise be imposed but mitigating circumstances exist, the person shall be exempted from sanction.

Article 15 Where disciplinary or illegal acts are minor and the person has corrected after criticism and education, the sanction may be waived.

Article 16 Where, before the people's court makes a decision on a disciplinary sanction, the person has already been sentenced to criminal punishment, removed from office by recall, removed from office, or has resigned from a leadership position, and needs to be sanctioned according to these Regulations, the sanction shall be imposed based on the facts of the disciplinary or illegal act.

A person who has been sentenced to criminal punishment shall be given discharge from public employment in all cases.

Article 17 Where court staff commit disciplinary or illegal acts after retirement, or commit such acts during their tenure but have already retired before the sanction decision is made, no disciplinary sanction shall be imposed. However, if demotion, dismissal from post, or discharge from public employment would otherwise be warranted, the treatment enjoyed by the person shall be correspondingly reduced or revoked in accordance with regulations.

Article 18 Property obtained through disciplinary or illegal acts and property used for such acts shall be confiscated, recovered, or ordered to be returned or compensated. Confiscated or recovered property shall be turned over to the state treasury in all cases.

For positions, professional titles, educational degrees, academic degrees, awards, qualifications, etc. obtained through disciplinary or illegal acts, the relevant units or departments shall be advised to correct or revoke them in accordance with regulations.

Section 3 Lifting, Modification, and Revocation of Disciplinary Sanctions

Article 19 For sanctions other than discharge from public employment, if the sanctioned person shows repentance during the sanction period and commits no further disciplinary or illegal acts, the sanction shall be lifted upon expiration of the period.

After the sanction is lifted, promotion in pay grade, rank, or position shall no longer be affected by the original sanction. However, lifting a demotion or dismissal from post shall not be deemed restoration of the original rank or position.

Article 20 Under any of the following circumstances, the sanction decision shall be modified or revoked:

(1) Incorrect application of laws, regulations, or provisions of these Regulations;
(2) Incorrect determination of the facts or circumstances of the disciplinary or illegal act;
(3) Insufficient evidence to support the disciplinary or illegal facts on which the sanction is based;
(4) Investigation and handling violate statutory procedures, affecting the fair handling of the case;
(5) The sanction decision exceeds authority or constitutes abuse of power;
(6) Other circumstances where the sanction is inappropriate.

Article 21 Where a sanction decision is modified and requires adjustment of the sanctioned person's position, rank, or pay grade, such adjustment shall be made accordingly. Where a sanction decision is revoked, the person's rank and pay grade shall be restored, an appropriate position corresponding to the original position shall be arranged, and the person's reputation shall be rehabilitated within an appropriate scope. Where the person's salary and welfare are damaged due to a modified lighter sanction or revocation of the sanction, compensation shall be provided.

Chapter II Specific Provisions

Section 1 Acts Violating Political Discipline

Article 22 Spreading statements damaging the nation's reputation, or participating in assemblies, processions, demonstrations, or other activities aimed at opposing the state, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

If a person participated in the above activities due to being misled without knowing the truth, and shows genuine repentance after criticism and education, the sanction may be mitigated or waived.

Article 23 Participating in illegal organizations or engaging in strikes shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

If a person participated in the above activities due to being misled without knowing the truth, and shows genuine repentance after criticism and education, the sanction may be mitigated or waived.

Article 24 Violating the state's ethnic or religious policies, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

If a person participated in the above activities due to being misled without knowing the truth, and shows genuine repentance after criticism and education, the sanction may be mitigated or waived.

Article 25 Damaging the nation's honor or interests in foreign exchanges shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 26 Illegally leaving the country, or staying abroad without returning in violation of regulations, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 27 Obtaining permanent residency abroad or acquiring foreign nationality without approval shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Section 2 Acts Violating Case-Handling Discipline

Article 29 Violating regulations by arbitrarily refusing to accept cases that should be accepted, or illegally accepting cases that should not be accepted, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 30 Violating regulations by failing to recuse oneself when recusal is required, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

If, knowing that a litigation representative or defense counsel does not meet the requirements for acting as a representative or defense counsel, a person still permits them to act as such, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, dismissal from post shall be imposed.

Article 31 Violating regulations by meeting with parties, their defense counsel, representatives, or persons making solicitations shall be punished by a warning. If adverse consequences are caused, a demerit or serious demerit shall be imposed.

Article 32 Violating regulations by recommending or introducing lawyers or representatives to parties, or introducing cases to lawyers or other persons, shall be punished by a warning. If adverse consequences are caused, a demerit or serious demerit shall be imposed.

Article 33 Violating regulations by meddling in, interfering with, or inquiring about cases, or tipping off parties, interceding, or lobbying on their behalf, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 34 Intentionally failing to collect relevant evidence that should be collected in accordance with regulations, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 35 Intentionally failing to take measures such as appraisal, inspection, or preservation of evidence that should be taken in accordance with regulations, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 36 Intentionally failing to take property preservation measures or enforcement measures that should be taken in accordance with regulations, or intentionally failing to entrust relevant agencies for audit, appraisal, evaluation, or auction that should be entrusted according to law, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 37 Violating regulations by taking or lifting property preservation measures, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 38 Intentionally violating regulations by selecting audit, appraisal, evaluation, or auction agencies, or colluding with or instructing such agencies to engage in malpractice or fraud in audit, appraisal, evaluation, or auction activities, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 39 Intentionally violating regulations by taking compulsory measures shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 40 Intentionally destroying, tampering with, concealing, forging, or swapping evidence or other litigation materials shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Instigating or assisting others to commit perjury, or obstructing others from testifying, shall be punished by demotion or dismissal from post. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 41 Intentionally concealing material evidence or important circumstances from the collegial panel or the adjudication committee, or providing false information, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 42 Intentionally disclosing specific details of the deliberations or discussions of cases by the collegial panel or the adjudication committee, or other secrets of trial or enforcement work, shall be punished by a demerit or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 43 Intentionally perverting the law in adjudication by deliberately distorting facts and law shall be punished by demotion or dismissal from post. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 44 For personal gain, violating regulations by forcing a party to withdraw a lawsuit, accept mediation, or reach a settlement agreement against their true will, thereby harming their interests, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 45 Intentionally violating regulations by taking enforcement measures, causing property loss to parties, non-parties, or third persons, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 46 Intentionally violating regulations by suspending, staying, terminating enforcement of a case that meets enforcement conditions, or failing to resume enforcement in accordance with law, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 47 Intentionally violating regulations by delaying case handling shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 48 Intentionally delaying or refusing to execute resolutions of the collegial panel or decisions of the adjudication committee, as well as judgments, rulings, decisions, or orders of the higher people's court, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 49 Illegally releasing a detained person shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 50 Violating regulations by privately handling cases shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Colluding with others to fabricate a case shall be punished by demotion, dismissal from post, or discharge from public employment.

Article 51 Forging litigation or enforcement documents, or intentionally making litigation or enforcement documents contrary to the resolutions of the collegial panel or decisions of the adjudication committee, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Delivering litigation or enforcement documents intentionally not in accordance with regulations, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit.

Article 52 Violating regulations by lending case files or other litigation materials to others shall be punished by a warning. If adverse consequences are caused, a demerit or serious demerit shall be imposed.

Article 53 Refusing to handle or intentionally delaying matters lawfully entrusted by a people's court of another locality, causing adverse consequences, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed.

Obstructing or interfering with a people's court of another locality in lawfully conducting investigation or evidence collection, or taking relevant property preservation measures, enforcement measures, or compulsory measures, shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 54 Other acts violating case-handling discipline shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Section 3 Acts Violating Integrity Discipline

Article 55 Taking advantage of official positions to illegally occupy litigation fees, enforcement funds or property, fines or confiscated property, case deposits, illicit money or goods and their proceeds, or other public property, through means such as embezzlement, theft, or fraud, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 56 Taking advantage of judicial authority or other official convenience to extort property or other property interests from others, or illegally accepting property or other property interests from others in exchange for seeking benefits for them, shall be punished by a serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Taking advantage of judicial authority or other official convenience to seek benefits for others, and illegally accepting property from others in the form of purchasing at a low price, selling at a high price, accepting shares without contribution, cooperative investment, entrusted financial management, gambling, or through a specific relationship by "name-only" receiving compensation or accepting property, or violating regulations by accepting kickbacks or handling fees in various names for personal ownership, shall be handled in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 57 Engaging in bribery or introducing bribes shall be punished by a demerit or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Bribing or introducing bribes to trial or enforcement personnel shall be given a heavier sanction in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 58 Misappropriating litigation fees, enforcement funds or property, fines or confiscated property, case deposits, illicit money or goods and their proceeds, or other public property, shall be punished by a demerit or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Article 59 Accepting property, banquets, or other benefits from parties, relevant intermediary agencies, or their principals shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit. If the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or dismissal from post shall be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, discharge from public employment shall be imposed.

Borrowing money or property from parties, relevant intermediary agencies, or their principals in violation of regulations shall be punished by a warning, demerit, or serious demerit.

Article 60 Where litigation fees, execution funds, fines and confiscated funds, case deposits, illegal proceeds and stolen goods and their proceeds, or other case-related property or public property are collectively intercepted, used, or distributed in the name of the unit, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 61 Where, by taking advantage of judicial authority, sponsorship is solicited or property is collected from citizens, legal persons, or other organizations in the name of the unit, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 62 Where fees are intentionally set up, the scope of fees is expanded, or the fee standards are raised in violation of regulations, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 63 Where, in violation of regulations, profit-making activities are engaged in, or a concurrent post is held in an enterprise or other profit-making organization, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 64 Where, by taking advantage of judicial authority or other job convenience, illegitimate benefits are sought for a specific person with a close relationship, or a specific person with a close relationship or a staff member in the immediate vicinity is allowed to use the official's authority to seek illegitimate benefits, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 65 Where there are other acts violating the discipline of integrity, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Section 4: Acts Violating Organizational and Personnel Discipline

Article 66 Where, in violation of rules of procedure, an individual or a minority decides on a major matter, or alters a major decision made collectively, resulting in a decision-making error, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 67 Where a superior's legally made decision or resolution is deliberately delayed or refused to be executed, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 68 Where a major accident or incident occurring within the scope of duties is not reported or handled in accordance with regulations, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 69 Where disciplinary or legal violations occurring within the scope of duties are concealed, not investigated, shielded, or covered up, or where a disciplinary or legal case assigned by a superior is deliberately delayed or refused to be handled, a major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 70 Where criticism is suppressed, retaliation is carried out, reporting letters are withheld or destroyed, or the content of a report is disclosed to the reported person, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 71 Where, in the work of personnel recruitment, hiring, assessment, promotion of posts, promotion of ranks, evaluation of professional titles, or job adjustments, favoritism is practiced or fraud is committed, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 72 Where fraud is committed to obtain honors, or false reports are made on educational background, degree, or professional title, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 73 Where an exchange decision of the organ is refused to be executed, or, when leaving office, resigning, or being dismissed, the transfer of official duties is refused to be handled, or an audit is refused to be accepted, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 74 Where absence from work without leave, or failure to return after an official trip or after the expiration of leave without justifiable reasons, results in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 75 Where an improper method is used to seek an overseas trip for oneself or a specific person with a close relationship at public expense, or the period abroad or outside the territory is arbitrarily extended, or the route is arbitrarily changed, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 76 Where there are other acts violating organizational and personnel discipline, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Section 5: Acts Violating Fiscal and Economic Discipline

Article 77 Where, in violation of regulations, material procurement or project bidding is carried out, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 78 Where a bank account is arbitrarily opened in violation of regulations or an "off-the-books account" is set up, a warning shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed.

Article 79 Where financial account books, accounting vouchers, or financial accounting reports are forged, altered, concealed, or destroyed, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 80 Where state funds are squandered or wasted in violation of regulations, a warning shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed.

Article 81 Where there are other acts violating fiscal and economic discipline, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Section 6: Acts of Dereliction of Duty

Article 82 Where, due to negligence, a case that should be accepted is not accepted, or a case that should not be accepted is illegally accepted, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed.

Article 83 Where, due to negligence, an erroneous judgment is made, erroneous property preservation measures, compulsory measures, or enforcement measures are taken, or necessary property preservation measures, compulsory measures, or enforcement measures are not taken, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if serious consequences result, demotion, removal from office, or dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 84 Where, due to negligence, the handling of a case seriously exceeds the prescribed time limit, resulting in serious consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed.

Article 85 Where, due to negligence, a person in custody escapes, self-injures, commits suicide, or injures another person, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if serious consequences result, demotion, removal from office, or dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 86 Where, due to negligence, the contents of litigation or enforcement documents are erroneous, resulting in serious consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed.

Article 87 Where, due to negligence, state secrets, trial and enforcement work secrets, other work secrets, trade secrets obtained in the course of performing duties, or personal privacy are leaked, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 88 Where, due to negligence, case files or evidence materials are damaged or lost, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if serious consequences result, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed.

Article 89 Where, due to negligence, a criminal case, a major public security case, a major social mass incident, or a major casualty accident occurs within the scope of duties, causing heavy losses to public property, the state, and the interests of the people, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 90 Where there are other acts of dereliction of duty resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Section 7: Acts Violating Management Order and Social Morality

Article 91 Where, due to slack work style or poor work attitude, adverse consequences result, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed.

Article 92 Where state secrets or work secrets are intentionally disclosed, or trade secrets or personal privacy obtained in the course of performing duties are intentionally disclosed, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 93 Where fraud is committed to mislead or deceive leaders and the public, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 94 Where, due to excessive drinking, normal work is affected or other adverse consequences result, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 95 Where, in violation of regulations, special items such as firearms, ammunition, or police equipment are kept or used, resulting in adverse consequences, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 96 Where, in violation of regulations on the management and use of official vehicles, a serious traffic accident occurs or other adverse consequences result, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 97 Where the execution of official duties is obstructed or, in violation of regulations, the execution of official duties is interfered with, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 98 Where the personal rights of another person are infringed upon by means such as beating, abusing, corporal punishment, unlawful detention, defamation, or false accusation, a demerit or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Where persons in custody are subjected to corporal punishment or maltreatment, or participants in proceedings or petitioners are beaten or verbally abused, a heavier sanction shall be imposed in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 99 Where adultery with another person results in adverse influence, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Where an improper sexual relationship occurs with a party to a case handled by the official or with a relative of such a party, a heavier sanction shall be imposed in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 100 Where bigamy is committed or a mistress or paramour is kept, removal from office or dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 101 Where the obligation to support, raise, or maintain is refused, or family members are maltreated or abandoned, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 102 Where drugs are ingested or injected, or participation in prostitution, solicitation of prostitution, or obscene and promiscuous activities occurs, removal from office or dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 103 Where participation in gambling occurs, a warning or demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, a major demerit or demotion shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, removal from office or dismissal shall be imposed.

Where a venue or other conveniences are provided for gambling activities, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Where gambling occurs during working hours, a demerit, major demerit, or demotion shall be imposed; if the individual refuses to correct despite repeated education, removal from office or dismissal shall be imposed.

Where public funds are misappropriated for gambling, removal from office or dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 104 Where participation in superstitious activities results in adverse influence, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed.

Where superstitious activities are organized, a demotion shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 105 Where childbirth beyond the plan is carried out in violation of regulations, a demotion shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Article 106 Where there are other acts violating management order and social morality, a warning, demerit, or major demerit shall be imposed; if the circumstances are relatively serious, demotion or removal from office shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, dismissal shall be imposed.

Chapter III: Supplementary Provisions

Article 107 For the purposes of these Regulations, "personnel of the People's Court" refers to personnel within the administrative establishment of the People's Court.

Personnel within the public institution establishment of the People's Court shall be governed by reference to these Regulations.

These Regulations shall not apply to personnel employed by the People's Court.

Article 108 For the purposes of these Regulations, "specific person with a close relationship" refers to a person who has a close relative, lover, or other close relationship with a personnel member of the People's Court.

Article 109 For the purposes of these Regulations, the terms "above" and "below" include the number itself.

Article 110 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 111 These Regulations shall take effect as of the date of promulgation. The "Several Provisions on Disciplinary Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Court (Trial)", the "Measures for Disciplinary Sanctions for Trial Work of the People's Court (Trial)", the "Measures for Disciplinary Sanctions for Enforcement Work of the People's Court (Trial)", and the "Several Provisions on Strictly Implementing the Relevant Disciplinary System of the 'Judges Law of the People's Republic of China'" previously promulgated by the Supreme People's Court shall be simultaneously abrogated.
